chapters.title: Unit 1: Marine Life & Sea Turtles
chapters.description: Prose: Sea Turtles, Poem: The Crocodile by Lewis Carroll, Supplementary: Owlie by Vijaya Ghose, Grammar: Nouns, Subject & Predicate, Prefixes.

concepts.title: Sea Turtles & Marine Life
concepts.summary: Seven species of sea turtles exist globally; five visit Indian waters. They return to nesting beaches through mass arribada.
key_points: Seven species worldwide; five in Indian waters (Olive Ridley, Hawksbill, Green Sea Turtle, Loggerhead, Leatherback).
Leatherback is the largest sea turtle, growing up to 2.2 meters and 700 kg.
Females come ashore only at night to lay eggs in deep sand pits.
Odisha coast is world-famous for mass nesting arribada.

concepts.title: Poetry: The Crocodile & Vocabulary
concepts.summary: Lewis Carroll's humorous poem depicting a crocodile on the Nile welcoming little fishes in with gently smiling jaws.
key_points: Poet: Lewis Carroll, renowned author of Alice in Wonderland.
Themes: Deception, predator instincts portrayed with playful rhyme.
Vocabulary: Doth (does), grin, scales, claws, smiling jaws.

chapters.title: Unit 2: Nature & When the Trees Walked
chapters.description: Prose: When the Trees Walked by Ruskin Bond, Poem: Trees by Joyce Kilmer, Supplementary: The Apple Tree and the Farmer, Grammar: Adjectives & Degrees of Comparison.

concepts.title: When the Trees Walked & Forest Conservation
concepts.summary: Grandfather's passion for planting saplings transforms a rocky riverbed into a vibrant green oasis for birds and animals.
key_points: Plants seek light and water, stretching their roots toward nutrients.
Planting trees prevents soil erosion and creates habitats for wildlife.
Ruskin Bond reflects on returning to find grandfather's saplings grown into a forest.

concepts.title: Grammar: Degrees of Comparison
concepts.summary: Using positive, comparative, and superlative degrees of adjectives to compare people, places, and things.
key_points: Positive degree: describes one noun without comparison (tall).
Comparative degree: compares two nouns, usually ending in -er or with 'more' (taller).
Superlative degree: compares three or more nouns, usually ending in -est or with 'most' (tallest).

chapters.title: Unit 3: World Cultures & Spices
chapters.description: Prose: A Visitor from Distant Lands, Poem: I Dream of Spices by Raj Arumugam, Supplementary: Stone Soup, Grammar: Prepositions & Sentence Types.

concepts.title: Global Spice Trade & History
concepts.summary: How ancient explorers sailed across oceans in search of Indian black pepper, cloves, and cardamom.
key_points: Black pepper was valued like black gold in ancient Rome and Greece.
Vasco da Gama reached Calicut (Kozhikode) in Kerala in 1498 seeking spices.
Chilies, potatoes, and tomatoes were introduced to India from South America via Portuguese traders.

concepts.title: Grammar: Prepositions and Sentence Structure
concepts.summary: Prepositions denote relationships of time, place, and direction between nouns and other words in a sentence.
key_points: Prepositions of place: on, under, between, behind.
Prepositions of time: in the morning, at 5 o'clock, on Monday.
Four sentence types: Declarative, Interrogative, Imperative, and Exclamatory.
